research_rationale: EO 2954 (September 13, 1918, Woodrow Wilson), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan text (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false; printed '[No. 2954.]', 'WOODROW WILSON', 'THE WHITE HOUSE, 13 September, 1918'). Under the Trading with the Enemy Act as amended March 28, 1918, it recites that the Alien Property Custodian's representative in the Philippines offered the property known as Froehlich & Kuttner for sale at Manila in May 1918, that Compania Mercantil de Filipinas bid it in, and that the Custodian disapproved the sale as not advertised or conducted under the prescribed rules; it then 'declare[s] the said sale to be void and of no effect' and 'authorize[s] and direct[s] the Alien Property Custodian to reject all bids received at the said sale', followed by five numbered reasons. The type rule TR-ALIEN-PROPERTY-SALE (drafted, awaiting review) says a rejection-of-bids order is spent when issued; under the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling that pattern cannot supply an end without evidence. The declaration of voidness took effect on signature, but the direction to the Custodian is a command to act, and no held source shows when, or whether, the Custodian rejected the bids or what became of the property (the order says the firm should have been liquidated under a War Trade Board license). The WPA 1944 list cites 'APC 540', a page of the Alien Property Custodian's report, which is not held. The dossier's clause inventory is also wrong: its three clauses (characters 2270-3002) are reasons (2), (3) and (5), which command nothing, and it omits the operative declaration and direction (characters 1564-1812 of the held text).

research_rationale: EO 6013 (February 3, 1933, Herbert Hoover). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 6998, its date (March 30, 1935) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It exempts Harry O. Bailey, Superintendent of Meters, Office of the Architect of the Capitol from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until April 1, 1937. It recites that Bailey was exempted for two years by EO 6088 of March 29, 1933 and 'further' exempts him. The WPA 1944 list dates this order March 25, 1935; the APP page, the census register and the recital in EO 7597 ('No. 6998 of March 30, 1935') give March 30, 1935, which this claim uses. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1937-04-01, inclusive. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 7597 (March 31, 1937) recites EO 6088 and EO 6998 ('periods totaling four years') and further exempts Bailey until July 1, 1937. Each recites this order as past history and grants a new period; none revokes or amends this order, so none is this order's end.
